t: Introduction and overview — RC-135 Rivet Joint
name: Introduction and overview — RC-135 Rivet Joint — aircraft record
title: Introduction and overview — RC-135 Rivet Joint
description: Signature-original re-engineering study: introduction and overview of the RC-135 Rivet Joint. This is a Signature-original design study, explicitly labeled and never presented as public record. Baseline reference: Signals-intelligence aircraft; service from the 1960s; ~17 RC-135V/W in U.S./UK service.. The RC-135 Rivet Joint is a four-engine signals-intelligence aircraft built by Boeing, entering service in the 1960s with continuous upgrades since. It collects electronic emissions near denied areas, feeding intelligence to commanders in near real time. About 17 RC-135V/W aircraft serve the U.S. Air Force and RAF. Signature improvements explored here: Signature composite primary structures cut empty weight ~12% versus the public baseline; Signature avionics suite with predictive-maintenance health monitoring on every major system. Angle: What this aircraft is, its role, and why it matters in aviation history.
how_it_works: Wings generate lift from airflow; the engine provides thrust; control surfaces and fly-by-wire or mechanical controls steer the aircraft in three axes.
